_comment: The five technical disputes that parked an Agent PR for a human on the first Target Project
(Smart-Smoker-V2 PRs 720, 721 and 723, 2026-10-04) under the old reconcile shape: every one a
bot-authored defect thread the implementer disputed, and every one the human later sided with
the implementer on. Each is scored against the Arbiter's escalation test
(plugin/agents/arbiter.md): (a) the issue and Spec are silent or contradict each other on the
point; (b) the options differ in behaviour a user of the Target Project would see. A dispute is a
product ambiguity iff BOTH hold; otherwise, and when unsure, the Arbiter rules. The expected
outcome of every entry is `ruled` (issue #77 AC 4). The run is an agent run: `bash
lib/arbiter-fixture.sh render` builds the Arbiter's prompt from these entries and `bash
lib/arbiter-fixture.sh check <reply>` reads the agent's verdicts through the runbook's own reader;
lib/arbiter-fixture.test.sh pins the fixture's consistency and both halves, with no model.

disputes.finding: Scope creep: reviewRows(..., now) becomes reviewRows(..., { now }) here and in extractionContract.test.ts, repairing skew between #717 and #718; a needed fix but not listed under #705's Interface changes. Failure scenario: No runtime failure; the PR carries an unrelated call-signature repair that a reviewer of #705 would not expect and that is not covered by its acceptance criteria.
disputes.dispute: master's reviewRows already takes a VoiceFillContext in every overload while master's session.ts still passes a bare Date, so reverting to reviewRows(..., now) would not typecheck on this branch. The signature repair has to ride with this PR or land separately first.
disputes.why: The Finding itself says 'No runtime failure'; the point is whether a compile-required call-site repair rides with the PR. The Spec is not silent on anything a user sees, and the branch does not typecheck without it. A technical call.

disputes.finding: Scope creep (defensible): rawByTranscript on the fake extractor goes beyond the spec's 'scriptable delay, failure and permission refusal', though it serves Behaviors to test 4. Failure scenario: No runtime failure; the fake adapter surface grows beyond the listed interface changes and later slices may come to depend on an unspecified scripting hook.
disputes.dispute: rawByTranscript is what lets the fake extractor answer a fixed transcript differently from the heard one; the issue's Behaviour 4 test ('editing the transcript and re-reading produces new rows') depends on it in both the session and pre-smoke suites, so removing it would drop that coverage.
disputes.requirement_quoted: Behaviors to test 4: editing the transcript and re-reading produces new rows
disputes.why: A test-double surface. The issue asks for the behaviour the hook makes testable, nothing a user sees changes either way. A technical call.

disputes.finding: Voice Fill is offered whenever models are provided; nothing checks that a cook is in progress, so the button is absent after finish only because the step unmounts. Failure scenario: Finish the cook, then tap the Post-Smoke segment on the completion screen: the step remounts on a cleared session and the button is back, against the AC 'absent once the cook is finished'. Filling a rest there sets restMinutes with no current smoke, so leaving the step calls saveServePlan with no cook. Path not run; typing in that state does the same and the wizard treats it as starting the next cook, so this may be intended.
disputes.dispute: the finished cook's step unmounts with it (tested); a segment tapped on the completion screen starts the next cook by design (smoke.tsx handleStep), where typing works and the backend upserts a new session, and the pre-smoke tracer gates on models only, so a cook-presence gate would hide Voice Fill on a live next-cook screen.
disputes.requirement_quoted: AC: absent once the cook is finished
disputes.why: The options do differ for a user (a button present or absent on the next-cook screen), but the Spec is not silent or self-contradicting: the AC is met on the finished cook's own step, and the completion-screen segment is by the Target Project's own design the start of the next cook, where the sibling pre-smoke step already offers Voice Fill gated on models only. One condition only: ruled.

disputes.finding: Scope creep: unrelated { now } change to the reviewRows call sites (session.ts:76-77 and extractionContract.test.ts), not asked for by #708. Failure scenario: The change is outside the issue's scope and the PR itself says session.ts will conflict textually with #720/#721, so whichever lands second needs a manual resolution.
disputes.dispute: the { now } change looks required rather than scope creep — master's reviewRows takes a VoiceFillContext while master's own call sites in session.ts and extractionContract.test.ts still pass a bare Date; with those two files reverted to master, 10 tests fail in session.test.ts and extractionContract.test.ts.
disputes.why: Same repair as pr720-reviewrows-signature seen from a sibling PR: ten tests fail without it, nothing a user sees changes with it. A technical call.

disputes.finding: The `|| !models` / READY fallback covers 'ports without a library', which the app never produces because VoiceFillModels always provides both. Failure scenario: If a later Slice does mount ports without a library, the Voice Fill button renders as ready with no readiness check at all. Judgement call.
disputes.dispute: 'ports provided with no library offers the button' is the contract of the merged tracer test (preSmokeStep.voiceFill.test.tsx, #718) and of smokeStep.voiceFill.test.tsx on feat/issue-707; removing the fallback here would break those sibling tests with no textual conflict, and the app itself never mounts ports without a library.
disputes.why: The Finding names a hypothetical later Slice, not a path the app produces; the fallback is the contract of merged sibling tests. Nothing a user sees differs today. A technical call.
